Layer 1 The World Bank through its Hope for Indigenous Family Support Initiative is supporting the Federal Government to implement the Nigeria Family Strengthening and Development Programme (NFSP) using the Social Safety Net System to identify poor and vulnerable Nigerian households for social intervention programmes, including the ₦100,000 Nigeria Family Support Programme NFSP.
The Programme , coordinated by the Hope for Indigenous Family Support Initiative’s Coordinating Office as mandated by the Federal Ministry of Youth Development is a Nigeria grassroots empowerment, and social intervention initiative programme under President Tinubu addressing economic hardship, rising food prices and the impacts of necessary economic reforms and subsidy removals. The Nigeria Family Strengthening and Development Programme (NFSP) is a cash transfer programme. It aims to mitigate the adverse effects of economic reform measures for the most vulnerable families in Nigeria.
The Initiative’s role came into focus following the Federal Government’s announcement through the Federal Ministry of Youth Development of the NFSP programme on September 10, 2026, under which selected beneficiaries are to receive ₦100,000 in family financial support.
Announcing the intervention, the Federal Ministry of Youth Development, said it was designed to ease the burden of rising living costs on vulnerable households.0:12 / 1:0
The integration of NIN records is expected to strengthen identity verification, reduce duplication and improve the accuracy of household information used for the social intervention programme.
The Federal Ministry through the Hope for Indigenous Family Support Initiative has clarified that selection is based on verified identity records and other relevant family and employment information for the NFSP cash transfer. the selection process involves:
1.Identifying eligible households through the Social Safety Net Systems.
3.Assessing households based on poverty and vulnerability criteria.
4.Selecting beneficiaries in phases across the six geopolitical zones.
The programme covers a finite number of households in each phase. This means beneficiaries will not all receive payments at the same time. If you have not received a notification, it does not necessarily mean you have been permanently excluded from the programme. How Will the ₦100,000 Cash Transfer Be Paid?
Payments are processed and payed to beneficiaries submitted bank accounts : Selected beneficiaries will receive an SMS notification from their designated payment provider. The phone number used for the notification will be obtained from the records used during the beneficiary selection process. Recipients are expected to follow the instructions in the message and provide the required consent before the money is credited to their submitted bank accounts. Who Is Eligible for the NFSP ₦100,000 Cash Transfer?
Must be a Nigerian citizen by birth. Must have National Identification number NIN as a valid form of identification to be validated with NIMC. Must be at least 18-65 years old at the time of registration.
The programme targets poor and vulnerable households identified through the Social Safety Nets Systems and verified national identity records. Selection is based on the government’s poverty and vulnerability criteria.
The official registration portal is nfsp.ng/signup where individuals can submit their details to become beneficiaries.
The Federal Ministry of Youth and Development has advised Nigerians to be careful of individuals and bloggers defaming and attacking the credibility of the program and also claiming they can secure access to the cash transfer. Take note of the following: The Nigeria Family Strengthening and Development Program NFSP is a social intervention and development programme .
3. Do not pay an individual or agent to release your ₦100,000 grant.
4. Not receiving a message immediately does not mean you have been permanently excluded.
5. The programme involves a structured process designed to identify households facing poverty and vulnerability.
For inquiries or further clarification, beneficiaries should contact the official NFSP official email [email protected] or through the Federal ministry’s recognized communication channels. Nigerians do not need to register through an unofficial website or pay anyone to qualify for this intervention. Beneficiaries are selected through the official NFSP registration portal’s social safety systems and verification process. SIGNED: MANAGEMENT BOARD
